rationale: The plan correctly uses DESeq2 Wald on ~condition with apeglm shrinkage and edgeR QL as a check, does not deduplicate, and keeps sample_01 in the primary analysis, so the core method and normalization are sound. It falls short of the reference on library-type-aware QC: it never computes rRNA fraction, mitochondrial fraction, or intronic share to explain the >60% duplication, instead declaring duplication 'not correctable post hoc,' and it does not consider removing rRNA/mt genes when their share is uneven. The contrast statement is garbled ('treated as the reference-vs-treatment contrast'), leaving the reference level ambiguous. Enrichment was not asked for and is not warranted; it is executed reasonably (Wald-stat ranking, versioned WikiPathways, minSize) but lacks a maxSize window and adds unrequested scope.
